Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

respect noun

an aspect, a way

also in this respect, in every respect, in some respects, in many respects, with respect to, in that respect

classical

Cic. Lael. 79: quod sit omnī ex parte in suō genere perfectum
Cic. Att. 7.3.3: ex parte magnā tibi adsentior

pars, partis f.

noun, third declension

part; in phrases, a respect: omnī ex parte, in every respect

Lewis & Short: omnī (ex, ā) parte, “in every respect, entirely”; ex magnā parte, in great part; in omnēs partēs, in every respect (Cic. Att. 11.6.2).

Other words

  • quod ad … attinet — with respect to, as regards

    phrase: attinet with ad and the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.14.4: hominem, quod ad mē attinet, nōn ingrātum; Plancus in Cic. Fam. 10.9.2: quod ad mē attinet, mī Cicerō

    See concern (be about).

Examples

  • nec quicquam difficilius quam reperīre quod sit omnī ex parte in suō genere perfectum

    and nothing is harder than to find something perfect of its kind in every respectCic. Lael. 79

  • habet enim rēs dēlīberātiōnem; etsī ex parte magnā tibi adsentior

    for the matter needs thinking over, though in many respects I agree with youCic. Att. 7.3.3

  • Brundisī jacēre in omnīs partīs est molestum.

    Lying idle at Brundisium is irksome in every respect.Cic. Att. 11.6.2

See also concern, part, respect.
